#### 1. hereditary breast carcinoma  —  Tier 1 — Definitive / Highly Plausible  (fitness 0.780)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-2559584, Reactome:R-HSA-2559586, Reactome:R-HSA-390471, Reactome:R-HSA-5693565, Reactome:R-HSA-6785807)

**Proposed mechanism:** TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ apoptosis (GO:0006915); TP53 (HGNC:11998) —DISRUPTS→ cell cycle regulation (GO:0051726); apoptosis (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Neoplastic progression (HP:0002664); cell cycle regulation (GO:0051726) —LEADS_TO→ Neoplastic progression (HP:0002664); apoptosis (GO:0006915) —LEADS_TO→ Breast carcinoma (HP:0002664); cell cycle regulation (GO:0051726) —LEADS_TO→ Breast carcinoma (HP:0002664). Loss-of-function mutations in TP53 disrupt critical tumor suppressive pathways, including apoptosis and cell cycle regulation, leading to neoplastic progression and specifically breast carcinoma in hereditary breast carcinoma, and a broader spectrum of cancers including breast cancer in Li-Fraumeni syndrome.

**How to falsify it:** Demonstration that pathogenic variants in TP53 are not enriched in either Li-Fraumeni syndrome or hereditary breast carcinoma cohorts, or that the identified variants in gnomAD have a minor allele frequency > 1% in relevant populations. _(variant: rs1295)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of TP53 in these conditions highlights potential therapeutic strategies targeting apoptosis and cell cycle regulation pathways, which could be beneficial for both Li-Fraumeni syndrome and hereditary breast carcinoma patients.
